1525128.steps:
1. Go to Network->Dynamic DNS, click Add button
  2. In the pop-up window, leave all check boxes in their default condition.
  3. Choose a service provider from the drop down Provider menu.
  4. Select a unique name for this profile (association) and enter it next to Profile Name:
  5. Enter the correct information for the account previously opened at this provider, to include: Username, Password and Domain Name.
  6. Click OK.k After configuration is updated, Wait at least 10 seconds and then refresh the DDNS page.
  7. Verify that the information line on the DDNS page for this new association presents the correct information as it was configured in (5), above and that the status indicates On-line: [your WAN IP] as of [todays date and time].
  8. Verify that the log contains an two INFO messages: DDNS association domain [your domain name] added and DDNS Update success for domain [your domain name] Online IP Updated. The correct IP addr should appear under Source IP Address with new domain
  9. Using your browser Intenet connection, go to the web site of the provider for the association just configured. Eg: http://www.dyndns.org for Dynamic DNS.
  10. Login to the account you (or Sonicwall QA) have created there and navigate to view the information for the association created above.
  11. Verify that the IP Address for the association is the WAN IP Addr of the SonicOS.
  12. On the PC, in a DOS window, type Ping [your domain name]
  13. Verify that ping is successful and that the IP Address indicated by Ping matches the IP Address of your domain.
  14. Repeat steps 1 thru 13 for each of the other 3 providers in the drop-down.
  15. Now, attempt to add an association with one or more invalid parameters eg wrong username, password or domain name.Repeat steps 1 thru 8 for each of the other 3 providers in the drop-down Select OK.
  16. After the configuration updates, refresh the GUI DDNS page and verify that the status shows Disabled (invalid account) as of [today] or similar.
  17. In the log, verify an error log message has been posted: DDNS Failure: Provider Chosen Provider reports account config error or invalid parameters .
  NOTE (Step 7): Depending on network traffic; ddns host site response time and other factors, it may take longer than 10 seconds for the correct OnLine status to appear. Re-refresh the page a few times if necessary.
  NOTE (Step 8): Due to compromises in the way the LOG code works, log messages for consecutively added associations may not be present in the log. The log will not store the SAME message more than once in any 60 second interval.
  NOTE (Step 13): In reality, it could take 5 minutes or more for the provider to update its records and for the records to propagate through the internet to various DNS servers. So, much leeway must be given here before calling this ping test a failure. Also, note that if the providers site indicates the proper parameters for your domain, then ping is actually just testing the Providers functionality of updating the DNS system with the new domain data, and is testing the Public Ping LAN server. So Ping test failures alone can not be used to fail the DDNS Test. Finally, ping failure could be due to a failure to configure the Public LAN Server for support of Ping testing

1525133.steps:
1. On the Network->Interfaces page, edit the WAN configuration by changing the IP Address to the Alternate IP Address. This is to assure no error messages from the ddns provider during testing.
  2. Create and verify a DDNS association in the manner described in TC 1, steps (1) thru (7). This can be one of the same3 associations, or a new one.
  3. On the Dynamic DNS GUI page, select the Configure icon for the association just created.
  4. On the Profile Tab of the resulting pop-up, change the profile name and select OK. Note: do NOT change any of the other fields at this time.
  5. After the configuration updates, wait 10 sec and refresh the GUI DDNS page. Verify that ONLY the Profile Name field has updated.
  6. On the PC, in a DOS window, type ping [the association domain name]'
  7. Verify that ping is successful and that the IP Address indicated by Ping matches your Alternate IP Address manually entered, above. On the Dynamic DNS GUI page , verify that the Profile Name field has updated.
  8. Repeat step (3)
  9. Select the Advanced tab on the resulting pop-up.
  10. Select the Specify IP Address manually Online Settings radio button.
  11. Enter the Original IP Address into the entry field.
  12. Select OK
  13. Wait 10 to 15 seconds, then refresh the GUI DDNS page.
  14. Verify that status for the chosen profile now contains the string: On-line: [Original IP Address] as of [todays date/time]..
  15. On the PC, in a DOS window, type ping [your domain name]'
  16. Verify that ping tries to reach the domain at the Original IP address, but is is NOT successful.
  17. Repeat steps (63) and (79)
  18. Select the Automatically set the IP Address to the Primary WAN Interface IP Address radio button. Press OK.
  19. Wait 10 to 15 seconds, then refresh the GUI DDNS page.
  20. On the Dynamic DNS GUI page, Verify that status for the chosen profile now contains the On-line: [Alternate IP Address] as of [todays date/time]Alternate IP Address, as configured in step (1).
  21. On the PC, in a DOS window, type ping [your domain name]'
  22. Verify that ping is successful and that the IP Address indicated by Ping matches the Alternate IP Address, ie The Primary WAN Interface, as above. (See NOTE (Step 13) TC1)
  23. Repeat steps 1 thru 22 for the remaining 3 providers.
